transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-06 17:30 UTC | Duration: 58m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Lina (Redwood SE), Marco (Gatekeeper Head ML), Nina (Platform), Aisha (PM), Tom (CISO)

Summary: Quick scoping for a 4-week POC focused on ops readiness, benchmarking latency/throughput, and an exec readout. Discussed access gates, sample workloads, success criteria, and ramp milestones.

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Um, quick roll call and then we'll walk through the proposed four week cadence.
00:22 Marco: Hey, Marco here. Sorry, I have a toddler in the background so might be ducking in and out.
00:30 Nina: Nina here, Platform Eng for Gatekeeper.
00:35 Aisha: Aisha, Product.
:40 Tom: Tom, CISO.
00:45 Jordan: Sweet. Lina and I are from Redwood — Lina will drive the benchmark bits.
01:05 Lina: Hi all. Quick agenda: kickoff & access, workload sizing + benchmarks, mid-point review mechanics, exec readout format, and success criteria.
01:30 Marco: Right, so high level we want to validate: A) sub-100ms median token latency for our chat-style assistant at target load B) can sustain 120 QPS with 4k token context on dedicated capacity C) cost per 1k tokens under $0.01 if possible, or show tradeoffs.
02:05 Jordan: Good, that's concrete. Lina, can you walk through the benchmark variants we recommend?
02:20 Lina: Sure. We'll do three lanes: 1) Hosted Redwood endpoint baseline with default batching 2) Dedicated reserved capacity with pinned model + autocaling disabled to measure steady throughput 3) Private in-VPC run (if you want to test crypto/KMS + network egress). We'll run synthetic traffic plus your real sample prompts. For metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost estimation, and failure modes.
03:10 Marco: For the private run, we need to know what the footprint is — GPUs, memory, and if KV cache is supported. We use a lot of 4k context KV ops.
03:32 Lina: We'll include a recommended hardware matrix: A100-40GB for baseline, then an eval path for 80GB models or quantized xformers on 80GB if you need throughput. KV/cache will be exercised; note that quantized routes change perf characteristics, slight degrades in p95.
04:05 Tom: Security checklist question — how do you handle KMS and audit logs in Redwood Private? Is HSM supported?
04:20 Jordan: Yes, we have KMS integrations and audit log exports; Private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM is available as an add-on. We'll send the SOC2 snapshot and the audit log format.
04:50 Tom: Also need SSO/SAML and RBAC controls for the console and service accounts.
05:05 Jordan: Yep, SSO + RBAC fine. We'll include proposed roles for read-only, ops, and admin.
05:30 Aisha: Back to timeline — you said 4 weeks. What's the ideal gating?
05:40 Lina: Week 0 (this week): kickoff + access. Week 1: ingest sample workloads, run initial microbenchmarks. Week 2: mid-point heavy benchmark (sustained QPS & latency) + ops test (failover, fallback to smaller model). Week 3: tweaks, cost regressions, final runs. End of week 4: exec readout with slides and runbook.
06:10 Marco: Ok, for access we need to know precise artifacts: service account with S3 read, sample id, and for Private we need VPN creds or VPC peering info.
06:25 Nina: We also require outbound firewall rules for the benchmark runner if hosted.
06:35 Jordan: We'll send an access checklist. I want to call out two critical success criteria you listed — latency and cost. We should encode them as pass/fail gates in the runbook.
07:05 Lina: Agreed. Example gates: Gate A (kickoff access): S3 & service account provisioned, sample dataset (>=100 conversations) available. Gate B (mid-point): p50 < 80ms, p95 < 250ms on 1k token average queries at 60 QPS sustained. Gate C (exec readout): < 10% quality regression vs baseline and cost under target or clear tradeoff plan.
08:00 Marco: That p95 target is aggressive but let's try. p50 80ms is reasonable for cached prefixes.
08:18 Jordan: We'll make sure benchmark harness includes prefix/KV caching simulation.
08:30 Lina: Note — caching can mask cold-starts, so we'll run cold and warm cache passes. Also show continuous batching behaviors.
09:05 Aisha: On stakeholder rhythm, who should get the mid-point readout? Engineering + Product + Ops and the exec owns the final.
09:15 Marco: Yes, Marco + Aisha + Nina for mid-point; Tom will join the exec readout to sign off on security posture.
09:30 Jordan: Great. I'll schedule two meetings: 90-minute mid-point deep-dive and 30-minute exec readout.
09:45 Marco: About datasets — we can provide 5 anonymized conversations and a synthetic corpus of 10k prompts. Is that enough?
10:00 Lina: That's perfect for functional evals and perf sampling. We'll also ask for a small unit of heavy-history threads to exercise long context.
10:20 Marco: For benchmarks, are you using open-source models or Redwood-verified ones?
10:30 Lina: We'll run the variants you agree to — often the baseline uses a Redwood-curated open variant for parity, dedicated uses a tuned release, and private can pin to a specific quantized artifact. We'll label them clearly in results.
11:00 Nina: Networking question — how do we handle subnet allocation and NAT egress on Private? We need a doc for our infra team to provision.
11:12 Jordan: We'll provide a VPC checklist with ports, subnets, and required routes; also an example CloudFormation/Terraform snippet.
11:30 Tom: About logs — we require immutable audit logs retention for 1 year, and alerts if keys rotate. Is that supported?
11:42 Jordan: Yes, audit export to your S3 or SIEM is supported. We'll include retention options and rotation hooks.
12:05 Aisha: Can we include a stakeholder success rubric for exec readout? Like one slide: latency, throughput, cost delta, and a recommended path to production.
12:20 Jordan: Absolutely. We'll craft an exec slide deck template.
12:40 Marco: On the benchmarking mechanics: what's your recommended traffic pattern? Constant, ramp, and burst?
12:50 Lina: We'll do steady-state at target QPS for 15 minutes, ramp to 2x for 5 minutes, and random bursts to emulate spikes. Also inject a fault (node failure) to test fallback.
13:20 Marco: How about result reproducibility — we'll want the scripts to be idempotent and logs saved.
13:30 Lina: We'll provide reproducible harness with a README and exact command lines; results uploaded to a shared spreadsheet.
14:00 Jordan: Cost modeling — we'll give two views: per-token cost and per-hour infra cost for dedicated. That way you can see unit economics.
14:20 Marco: We're also considering on-prem for latency-sensitive geos. How different will that be?
14:30 Lina: On-prem yields better network latency but ops overhead. We'll show the delta and highlight data residency benefits.
15:00 Tom: Any concerns about export controls or model weights staying on-prem?
15:10 Jordan: Private keeps model artifacts local if requested; we'll outline the flow.
15:30 Marco: Ok, timeline confirmation: kickoff today — access by Friday — initial microbench by next Thursday — mid-point by week 2.
15:48 Jordan: Correct. We'll set milestones on a shared board.
16:00 Aisha: Who owns the failover test? Decide if Redwood triggers fallback or we simulate degradations.
16:15 Lina: We'll run both: Redwood will trigger an internal fallback and you'll run a simulated node loss.
16:30 Marco: Can we include quality checks — like end-to-end correctness and hallucination rate?
16:40 Lina: Yes, we'll add top-n accuracy, hallucination counts, and a small annotation job. If quality regresses >10% we flag it as a blocker.
17:00 Tom: Security handshake — I'll expect an NDA addendum for private infra details.
17:10 Jordan: We'll route that to legal — add as an action item.
17:25 Jordan: Okay let's recap action items and owners.
17:35 Speaker 2: (brief cross-talk)
17:45 Marco: Sounds good. Thanks, everyone.
17:50 Jordan: Thanks — we'll follow up with the POC runbook, access checklist, and a calendar invite for mid-point.
18:00 Meeting ends.

Notes on transcription: There are a few mis-attributions (Speaker 2) and some garbled words where network jitter occurred. Several technical terms: KV cache, quantization, xformers, A100, KMS, HSM, SSO, RBAC were used (some auto-corrected).

Documents referenced (to be shared): POC runbook draft (link forthcoming), security checklist PDF, benchmark harness repo (private link), sample spreadsheet for results.

Exec readout plan (draft):
- Slide 1: TL;DR — did we meet latency & cost gates?
- Slide 2: Benchmark brief (p50/p95/p99 plus tokens/sec)
- Slide 3: Ops resilience tests and fallback behavior
- Slide 4: Security/compliance posture and next steps for Private
- Slide 5: Recommendation and path to production (short, medium, long term)

End of transcript.
